- Marissa: technical runbook + test plan for peering and endpoint NAT rules

Thanks Priya — quick answers and attachments below.

Preferred maintenance window: 2027-05-05 02:00-04:00 UTC (overnight maintenance for our east coast customers).
CIDRs for peering: 10.10.0.0/16 (prod), 10.20.0.0/16 (staging). No overlapping subnets.
Public ASN: 64512 (we'll handle BGP on our edge).
Firewall: our network ops team requires an ACL change request 48 hours in advance; contact is ops-requests@ironbridge.com. They also requested that Redwood provide a certificate thumbprint for any management endpoints.

I've attached our network diagram (ironbridge-network-diagram.pdf) and an initial MAM config dump (ironbridge-mam-config.yaml). Note: our egress inspection strips unknown headers — recommend we test the health check path for signature headers.

On the on-prem appliance: we plan to place it in our DMZ with NAT from 198.51.100.0/24. We'll need the appliance install bundle and a checklist for air-gapped validation.

Samir

Thanks Samir — very helpful. I've drafted a short peering runbook and a validation test plan. Summary of what we'll execute during the 2027-05-05 02:00-04:00 UTC window:
- Step 1: Establish peering and verify route advertisement (5-10 mins)
- Step 2: Configure private endpoint(s) on Redwood side; validate TCP/443 handshake to customer IPs (10-15 mins)
- Step 3: Run KV cache warm-up and model endpoint smoke test (we'll use synthetic prompt set) (15-20 mins)
- Step 4: On-prem appliance smoke test (if appliance shipped early) — otherwise defer to separate window
- Step 5: Rollback plan and validation (10 mins)

Open items for IronBridge (Samir):
- Confirm certificate thumbprint for management endpoints
- Provide ops-requests contact for immediate ticket escalation (we have ops-requests@ironbridge.com but want a direct on-call number)
- Confirm if there is a requirement for client IP allowlist vs. CIDR-based firewall rules

I'll attach the runbook and test plan to the ticket after we confirm the window.
